text: I. Professional Core PositioningMaterials are the material foundation for human production, life, and technological progress. From traditional metals, ceramics, and plastics, to battery materials in the field of new energy, high-temperature alloys in aerospace, and degradable materials for medical use, all fall within the scope of research in materials science and engineering. This major aims to explore the fundamental laws of materials, achieve "tailored design" and "efficient production", and promote innovative applications of materials in fields such as energy, environment, information, and healthcare.II. Training ObjectivesTo cultivate highly competent interdisciplinary senior talents who possess solid theoretical foundations in mathematics, physics, chemistry, etc., and master the basic principles of materials science (such as the relationship between material structure and performance) and engineering technology (such as material preparation, processing, and testing methods). These talents should be capable of engaging in scientific research, technological development, process design, production management, etc. in the fields of materials research, production, and application. Specific requirements include: Master the intrinsic connections among the composition, structure and properties of materials;Possess experimental skills in material preparation, processing, characterization and performance testing;Understand the latest developments in the field of materials and industrial demands, and possess innovative thinking and the ability to solve practical problems.
